purpose: Proposed V2 Central Water implementation visualization, not an engine capture
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: implementation-oriented terrain visualization for the Central Water layout in a low-poly industrial RTS game. Generate ONE landscape image, a plausible real-time engine screenshot without UI, rather than fantasy painterly concept art.
Scene: a complete square playable map viewed from a high oblique strategy camera. Four small industrial headquarters occupy generous dry opening areas around an irregular centrally enclosed lake. Continuous wide dry routes loop around BOTH sides of the lake and connect all four starts. There is NO ocean, no bridge, no ship, no river cutting off a base.
Terrain implementation: show a clearly legible uniform grid of SMALL square terrain cells, approximately 6 game units wide, with connected equal-height grassy interiors and fixed 2-unit elevation steps. The lake occupies about one fifth of the map, surrounded by spacious connected lowlands. Cell edges are evident through stepped geometric shorelines and occasional subtle material seams, not a black wireframe overlay. Preserve an irregular naturally derived contour across many small cells, not giant square platforms. Ordinary dry land is predominantly flat connected open ground, with only a few coherent low terraced hills around the outer areas and one compact rocky peak. Broad selected ramp corridors climb hills, each roughly one or two cell widths long for one elevation step, smoothly joined to flat landings. Short deliberate steep cliff sections have narrow bevels and no cracks. Avoid tall cliff forests, smooth sculpted hills, rectangular macro mesas, repetitive tiny ledges or a staircase covering the whole map.
Water implementation: ONE coherent horizontal blue lake surface above a visibly shallow stepped shore bed, gently varying transparent shallows, partially wet boundary cells, deeper center. Wet geometry follows the stepped bed; most lake banks are low, accessible shores rather than tall walls. Fully water-covered inner cells cannot host land structures. Show ONE small industrial land building near the foreground shoreline: its footprint mostly rests on connected dry flat land, with a small less-than-one-third corner over shallow water WITHIN a partially wet shore cell, visibly supported by short foundation piers reaching the bed. It must not span into a wholly wet tile or become a bridge. Keep the other buildings on dry level ground with reachable perimeter space.
Resources/scenery: several large irregular salvage clusters composed of scattered small scrap piles and occasional larger wrecks on dry land, sparse oil extraction pockets, grouped small trees with clearings. Opening resources visually nearby each base, but do not make resource density dominant. Keep dry roads, ramps, building space and shores legible.
Style: simple flat-shaded meshes with restrained textured surfaces, realistic gameplay scale, neutral bright daylight, clear orthographic-like perspective, readable silhouettes, whole map visible with camera tilted enough to expose stepped elevation and foundations. Small buildings help communicate that each square cell is far smaller than a headquarters footprint. No text, labels, HUD, watermark, fantasy structures, dramatic haze or artistic cliffs taller than the bases.
Intent: illustrate the proposed V2 geometry and layout faithfully, not claim it is a screenshot of already implemented code.
